In [[geometry]], the '''pentagonal bifrustum''' or '''truncated pentagonal bipyramid''' is the third in an infinite series of [[bifrustum]] polyhedra. It has 10 [[trapezoid]]al and 2 [[pentagon]]al faces.

==Constructions==
The pentagonal bifrustum is the [[dual polyhedron]] of a [[Johnson solid]], the [[elongated pentagonal bipyramid]]. {{Johnson solid}}

This polyhedron can be constructed by taking a [[pentagonal bipyramid]] and [[Truncation (geometry)|truncating]] the polar axis vertices. In [[Conway polyhedron notation]], it can be represented as the polyhedron "{{math|t5dP5}}", meaning the truncation of the degree-five vertices of the dual of a [[pentagonal prism]].<ref>[http://www.georgehart.com/virtual-polyhedra/conway_notation.html Conway Notation for Polyhedra], [[George W. Hart]], accessed 2014-12-20.</ref>

Alternatively, it can be constructed by gluing together two end-to-end pentagonal [[frustum]]s, or (if coplanar faces are allowed) by gluing together two pentagonal prisms on their pentagonal faces.

==Application==
In [[Nanoparticle|nanoparticles]], a 15-site truncated pentagonal bipyramid structure may form the [[Nucleation|nucleus]] of larger twinned structures with [[Fiveling|five-fold]] or [[Icosahedral twins|icosahedral]] symmetry.<ref>{{citation|journal=Materials Science Forum|volume=312–314|pages=325–332|doi=10.4028/www.scientific.net/MSF.312-314.325|first=Herbert|last=Hofmeister|title=Fivefold twinning in nanosized particles and nanocrystalline thin films – ubiquitous metastable structures|year=1999|s2cid=136620837|url=http://www.mpi-halle.mpg.de/mpi/publi/pdf/505_99.pdf}}.</ref>
